direct.title: The direct method
direct.subtitle: The dough is prepared in a single step
body: It's a simpler preparation method than the indirect ones.
All ingredients are incorporated at once and, after a shorter or longer rest, the dough is ready to use.

poolish.title: Poolish
poolish.subtitle: A liquid dough made of flour, water and yeast
body: Poolish is a pre-fermentation of the dough that rests for several hours before being used for the pizza dough.
It is prepared by mixing 1 part flour and 1 part water, with a small amount of yeast.
It's an indirect method of preparing pizza dough.

biga.title: Biga
biga.subtitle: A dry pre-fermentation made of flour, water and yeast
body: Biga is a pre-fermentation of the dough that rests for several hours before being used for the pizza dough.
Unlike poolish, it is a so-called dry preparation: its hydration sits around 45 to 50%.
It is prepared by roughly mixing the flour, water and yeast; it gives the dough strength and more complex flavours.

yeasts.title: Yeasts
yeasts.subtitle: The calculator offers three types of yeast
body: Active dry yeast is the "classic" baker's yeast found in shops — not the rapid kind. It is usually sold in sachets of small pellets.
Instant dry yeast is freeze-dried yeast in fine flakes. It doesn't need to be hydrated before use and allows quick rises.
Fresh yeast is the baker's yeast found in shops as a "fresh" paste, in cubes.
tips: The calculator makes it easy to switch from one yeast to another.

hydration.title: Hydration
hydration.subtitle: The ratio of total water to total flour
body: Ex. 1: with 100 g of total water and 151.5 g of total flour, the dough hydration is 66%. Calculation: 100 ÷ 151.5 = 0.66, i.e. 66%.
Ex. 2: to know how much water to add with 151.5 g of flour and a target hydration of 66%, the calculation is: 0.66 × 151.5 = 100 g of total water.
tips: The more hydrated the dough, the harder it is to handle: more liquid, therefore stickier. Recommended hydration: between 62 and 75%.

poolishRatio.title: Poolish ratio
poolishRatio.subtitle: The ratio of poolish to the total amount of dough
body: Between 30 and 60% of poolish is commonly used in the final dough quantity.
Ex.: for 30% poolish and 1 kg of final dough, the calculation is: 1000 × 0.3 = 300 g. The poolish will weigh 300 g, made of 150 g of flour and 150 g of water.
tips: A higher poolish ratio is generally used in winter than in summer, as fermentation is partly influenced by temperature: more poolish in winter can help the final development of the dough.

temperature.title: Temperature
temperature.subtitle: The ambient temperature of the room, outside the fridge
body: It's the temperature of the room where the poolish, the biga, the dough and the dough balls will rest.
It is used to compute the warm rest.

warmRest.title: Warm rest
warmRest.subtitle: The time spent at room temperature
body: The rest time of the various preparations at the selected room temperature.

coldRest.title: Cold rest
coldRest.subtitle: The time spent in the fridge
body: The rest time of the various preparations in the fridge.
